summary: The neighborhood council announced on September 15, 2023 a plan to upgrade local parks and playgrounds, shaped by community feedback. It includes age-specific zones, a splash pad, sports facilities, event spaces, eco-friendly features and free Wi-Fi, rolled out in phases from late 2023 to spring 2024. Residents and local figures voiced support, and town hall meetings are gathering public input.
one_line: The neighborhood council unveiled a phased 2023-2024 plan to upgrade parks and playgrounds with new play, sports, event, eco-friendly and Wi-Fi features.
key_facts: The neighborhood council announced the parks and playgrounds upgrade plan on September 15, 2023, at an unveiling event at Oakridge Park.
Councilwoman Elizabeth Rivera presented the plan, saying "Every family deserves a sanctuary in their backyard."
Construction is set to commence by late October 2023.
The first phase is expected to launch around Thanksgiving 2023, with major playground and landscaping upgrades to be completed by spring 2024.
The phased approach keeps some parts of the parks accessible during renovation to minimize disruption.
Planned features include new grass, trees and landscaping, age-specific zones, reading nooks with benches and book exchanges, modern playground equipment, and a new splash pad.
Sports upgrades include refurbished basketball courts, new outdoor fitness stations and outdoor chess tables, plus shaded areas for the elderly or those seeking tranquility.
Multi-purpose open areas will host small local festivals, outdoor yoga classes and neighborhood movie nights.
The first 'Town Hall' style meeting for resident input was held on September 30, 2023, and drew a sizable crowd.
Sustainability measures include recycled materials for playground equipment, solar-powered lights for pathways and playing areas, and water conservation systems.
Shaw Park is slated for one of the first major overhauls, with a new jungle gym replacing dilapidated equipment and new high-grade surfacing on its basketball courts.
Free Wi-Fi zones are planned across park facilities.
Quoted supporters include Michael Thompson, Jorge Martinez, Carla Sanchez, Amanda Lee, David Kim, Tyrone Biggs and Sara Johnson.
